clue.text: Really it is the quickest way to get high

definitions.meaning: used as an exclamation or adverb meaning honestly, no word of a lie

definitions.text: the quickest way to get high
definitions.meaning: going vertically, with no detour, is the fastest route upwards

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for the fastest route to a high, perhaps a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is' is the link joining the two definitions; 'get high' suggests drugs but means simply climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as an informal intensifier for honestly and as a direction meaning vertically.

clue.text: Second strip that's worn in summer

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A striptease performed in a second, but only in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless dress is a garment designed for warm sunny weather.

clue.text: Three-quarters of army group in administration

indicators.note: keep six of the eight letters of the synonym, dropping its final quarter

parts.note: a regiment is a unit or group of an army

explanation.surface: A military unit is part of a governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters of' trims the last two letters, NT, from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system of government or administration, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Determined where camper might be found

definitions.meaning: a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: A resolute holidaymaker sought under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set on doing something is to be resolved or determined about it.

clue.text: Her baring could be sign of what is to come

definitions.text: sign of what is to come

indicators.note: suggests the letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman exposing herself might portend trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HERBARING into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a forerunner or omen announcing an approaching event.

clue.text: Priest takes craftsman to be supporter of a cause

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A clergyman hires a craftsman who turns out to be a committed activist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link: P simply sits before ARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed adherent or champion of a party or cause.

clue.text: Warning: one may get passionate about nothing

indicators.note: the word for passionate goes around the letter for nothing

parts.note: hot means ardent or passionate
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A caution that someone may become heated over trifles.
explanation.definitionFit: A car horn's blast or toot is a sound used to alert people, a warning signal.

clue.text: Perhaps Snowdon's most memorable part?

parts.note: Snowdon is a mountain in Wales, so its summit is literally an elevated place, and also the best moment of a trip

explanation.surface: Asking which part of a Snowdon visit stood out most.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A high spot is the most enjoyable or outstanding moment of an experience.

clue.text: To repeat jazzed-up form of entertainment

indicators.note: jazzing something up livens and reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An encore given a jazz arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazzed-up' rearranges TOREPEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light comic opera, a kind of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Worthless weapon returned by a politician

indicators.note: sent back, so the weapon's word is read from the end

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A gun handed back by a politician proves useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GUN into NUG; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory is a formal adjective for something of no value or force, futile.

clue.text: Regretted overtaking child's horse, by the sound of it — that's rough

indicators.note: the word for regretted takes in another piece, swallowing it

parts.note: rued means regretted

indicators.note: the nursery word is spoken as its two letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone regretted passing a toddler's pony, which proved hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's horse' is the nursery word gee-gee, spoken as two letters; 'overtaking' is the container signal and 'that's' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged terrain is uneven and harsh, which is to say rough.

clue.text: Sentimental type having nervous reaction

parts.note: roman is the upright style of printing type
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A soppy person who twitches nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentimental type' reads as one noun phrase, but 'type' gives ROMAN; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes an idealised, emotional outlook, a synonym for sentimental.

clue.text: Marchers should be foot division?

definitions.meaning: soldiers marching should move in unison
a part of the foot, arch between toes and ankle

explanation.surface: Asking whether an infantry unit should keep in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot division' suggests infantry, but it is a part of the human foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched upper middle part of the foot is one region or division of it.

clue.text: Miss a festivity

parts.note: a miss is a girl, informally a gal

explanation.surface: Someone skips a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb but is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment.

clue.text: Sweet drink on the rocks?

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: A sugary drink served with ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; in a down clue the second piece sits under the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a black chewy confection, a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Imagine having drink with model

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Picturing a drink taken with a model.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or think something likely, to imagine it.

clue.text: A top duet performed that's modern

indicators.note: the letters are worked or acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A leading pair of singers sang something contemporary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges ATOPDUET; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means current, reflecting the latest fashion or knowledge.

clue.text: In abbey, technology is given precedence

indicators.note: the technology letters are placed within the abbey word

parts.note: a priory is a small abbey or monastery
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: Modern equipment takes first place in a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbey' suggests a grand church, but a priory is a small monastic house; 'is given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority is the right to go first, the same as precedence.

clue.text: Teams who arranged stall at fairground

parts.note: sides are opposing teams

indicators.note: the short word is put into a new order

explanation.surface: Teams set up a booth at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns WHO into HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a small booth or attraction at a fair, separate from the main event.

clue.text: Sign first letter only

definitions.meaning: to mark a document with one's abbreviated name
the opening letter of a name, all that is written

explanation.surface: An instruction to sign with just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To initial is to sign with abbreviated letters; an initial is a name's first letter.

clue.text: Cooking his meat first makes you irritable

indicators.note: the meat goes before the other piece

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to put meat in first, which annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' turns HIS into ISH; 'first' puts LIVER ahead; 'makes you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish is an old word for being peevish and bad-tempered, once blamed on a disordered liver.

clue.text: Regularly misread 'Queen and Country'

indicators.note: take every other letter of this word, starting with the second

parts.note: Q is a standard abbreviation for queen, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A title is said to have been misread.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of MISREAD give IRA; 'and' is a link joining Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a nation in the Middle East, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Black bird dog

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound breed, a kind of dog.

clue.text: Falling out on the lake?

definitions.meaning: a row is a quarrel, and the noun from arguing is a falling out
propelling a boat with oars on water

explanation.surface: Tumbling out of a boat on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing means quarrelling, and also means using oars, which one does on a lake.

clue.text: Playful little woman has company going to Kent maybe

parts.note: Jo is one of the March sisters in the novel Little Women
Kent is a county in south-east England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A frisky lady takes friends off to Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county in the South East; 'has' and 'going to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means given to joking, so humorous and playful.

clue.text: Advance twice — but be reasonable!

indicators.note: the word is written two times in a row

parts.note: to advance is to come forward

explanation.surface: An urging to step forward, twice, and be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a mild remonstrance asking someone to be sensible or stop exaggerating.

clue.text: Generous number from Rome having whip-round

indicators.note: the whip word goes around the Roman number

parts.note: a lash is a whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted figure from Rome organises a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but it splits into whip, LASH, and round, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means giving or spending freely, extravagantly generous.

clue.text: Heather, for all to see, at home before one making pasta

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come ahead of the final letter

parts.note: ling is a type of heather
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for everyone
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Heather, in full view at home, cooks Italian before guests.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a type of flat narrow ribbon pasta.

clue.text: Tax produces flippancy when it's dodged

indicators.note: the word is avoided, so it leaves the larger word

parts.note: levity is frivolous, flippant lightness
the word it, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A tax produces flippant jokes when people avoid it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodged' removes IT from LEVITY; 'produces' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a tax or charge imposed by authority.

clue.text: Shake and stretch? You'll get it if you're on mine

definitions.text: You'll get it if you're on mine

parts.note: to wave is to shake something to and fro
a length is a stretch of distance or time

explanation.surface: Someone claims you will understand them if you think alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'on the same wavelength', thinking alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on someone's frequency, in the idiom, means you understand them, so the definition describes it.
